'''Štefan Jánoš''' (also known as '''Stefan Janos'''; born 22 December 1943) is a Slovak-Swiss [[physicist]] and university [[professor]]. He is the founder of very [[low temperature physics]] in Slovakia.

== Life ==
Štefan Jánoš was born on 22 December 1943 in [[Kuchyňa]], [[Slovak Republic (1939–1945)|Slovak Republic]]. From 1950 to 1958, he attended the [[primary school]] in [[Suchohrad]] and [[Záhorská Ves]] and between 1958&ndash;1961 the [[high school]] in [[Malacky]]. Thereafter he studied at the Czech Technical University, [[Czech Technical University in Prague|Faculty of Technical and Nuclear Physics in Prague]]. In 1966 he graduated from university with diploma thesis " [[Specific heat]] of [[Iron|Fe]]–[[Cobalt|Co]] [[alloy]]s in the temperature range 1.4 to 4.2 [[Kelvin|K]]. He spent his one-year military service mainly at the Research and Test Centre of the Ministry of Defence in Brno. In August 1967 he joined the Faculty of Science at [[Pavol Jozef Šafárik University]] in [[Košice]]. There he started to build a new laboratory for very low temperature physics. Three years later he spent a study visit in Prof. [[Boris. N. Eselson]] laboratory in [[B Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine|National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in Kharkov]] . He participated in experiments on the influence of [[Helium-3|<sup>3</sup>He]] [[atom]]s on the [[Superfluidity|superfluid]] state of [[Helium-4|<sup>4</sup>He]] at 0.5 K. In 1972 he worked at the [[Aalto University]] of Helsinki in Prof. [[Olli Lounasmaa]] Low Temperature Laboratory in [[Otaniemi]], Finland. Together with [[Yuri D. Anufriev]] he participated in experiments on the search for superfluid state in 3He using [[Pomeranchuk cooling]]. He received his [[PhD]] in physics from P.J. Šafárik University, Košice, in 1976 under the supervision of Prof. [[Vladimir Hajko]]. His [[dissertation]] dealt with the [[magnon]] [[heat transfer]] in [[Rare-earth element|thulium and erbium-yttrium]] alloys between 0.4 K and 4.2 K and in [[magnetic fields]] up to 3 [[tesla (unit)|tesla]]. From 1980 to 1984 he was head of the Department of Low Temperature Physics in the [[Slovak Academy of Sciences|Institute of Experimental Physics of the Slovak Academy]] of Sciences (SAS) in Košice. His main research interests concentrated on superfluid 3He, [[nuclear cooling]], [[Spectroscopy|point-contact spectroscopy]] and [[cryogenic]] applications in [[ophthalmology]], [[gynaecology]] and [[plastic surgery]]. He constructed various cryogenic apparatus for [[cryosurgery]]. In 1982 he habilitated on thermal conductivity of [[Rare-earth element|Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu]] in the temperature range from 0.5 K to 10 K. Between 1984 and 1990 he worked at the Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics of the [[Comenius University]] in [[Bratislava]]. He held lectures on optics and low temperature physics. His scientific research focused on superfluid 3He and high-temperature [[superconducting]] [[Thin film|thin]] REBaCuO films (RE = [[Rare-earth element|Y, Dy, Ho, Gd, Sm, Nd, Eu]]).<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Kúš | first1=P. | last2=Jánoš | first2=Š. | title=Preparation of Gd-Ba-Cu-O superconducting thin films on SrTiO3, Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> and ZrO<sub>2</sub> by magnetron sputtering | journal=Modern Physics Letters B | publisher=World Scientific Pub Co Pte Lt | volume=02 | issue=10 | year=1988 | issn=0217-9849 | doi=10.1142/s0217984988001053 | pages=1151–1154| bibcode=1988MPLB....2.1151K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Kúš | first1=P. | last2=Jánoš | first2=Š. | title=Preparation of Gd-Ba-Cu-O superconducting thin films on silicon substrates by magnetron sputtering | journal=Modern Physics Letters B | publisher=World Scientific Pub Co Pte Lt | volume=03 | issue=1 | year=1989 | issn=0217-9849 | doi=10.1142/s0217984989000078 | pages=37–40| bibcode=1989MPLB....3...37K }}</ref> On 15 June 1990, as an [[assistant professor]], he joined the Laboratory for [[University of Bern|High Energy Physics of the University of Bern]] in Switzerland, which was headed by Prof. [[Klaus Pretzl]]. He took a leading role in the development of the SSG (Superconducting superheated granules) [[detector]] for low-energy [[neutrino]]s and [[dark matter]]. He took part in experiments using [[neutron]] [[Charged particle beam|beam]] to study nuclear recoil on [[Tin|Sn]], [[Zinc|Zn]] and [[Alumninum|Al]] nuclei conducted at the [[Paul Scherrer Institute]] in Switzerland. In his scientific work at the Laboratory for High Energy Physics in Bern he studied phase transition in Sn, Zn, In, and Al granules and also Al- and In- [[microstructure]]s using [[SQUID]] (Superconducting Quantum Interference Device). He took a leading role in the development, construction and installation of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20110707004312/http://www.lhep.unibe.ch/orpheus/orpheus_index.php?lang=en&id=1 ORPHEUS detector] for dark matter search in the Bern Underground Laboratory.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Borer | first1=K. | last2=Czapek | first2=G. | last3=Hasenbalg | first3=F. | last4=Hauser | first4=M. | last5=Janos | first5=S. | last6=Loaiza | first6=P. | last7=Moser | first7=U. | last8=Pretzl | first8=K. | last9=Schütz | first9=C. | last10=Wicht | first10=P. | last11=Wüthrich | first11=S. | title=First results with the ORPHEUS dark matter detector | journal=Astroparticle Physics | volume=22 | issue=2 | year=2004 | issn=0927-6505 | doi=10.1016/j.astropartphys.2004.06.005 | pages=199–210| arxiv=astro-ph/0404311 | bibcode=2004APh....22..199B | s2cid=9335366 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Janos | first1=S. | last2=Hauser | first2=M. | last3=Pretzl | first3=K. | last4=Nydegger | first4=F. | last5=Schütz | first5=H.U. | last6=Lehmann | first6=S. | last7=Hess | first7=M. | last8=Roulin | first8=J.C. | title=The Bern Cryogenic Detector System for dark matter search | journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=547 | issue=2–3 | year=2005 | issn=0168-9002 | doi=10.1016/j.nima.2005.03.155 | pages=359–367| bibcode=2005NIMPA.547..359J}}</ref> He held exercises and lectures for students of [[physics]] on [[mechanics]], [[electricity]], [[magnetism]] and [[modern physics]]. He also lectured on [[superfluidity]], [[superconductivity]] and physical properties of [[solids]] at low temperatures.
He participated in the discovery of the [[Lazarus effect]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Palmieri | first1=Vittorio Giulio | last2=Borer | first2=Kurt | last3=Janos | first3=Stefan | last4=Da Viá | first4=Cinzia | title=Evidence for charge collection efficiency recovery in heavily irradiated silicon detectors operated at cryogenic temperatures | journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=413 | issue=2–3 | year=1998 | issn=0168-9002 | doi=10.1016/s0168-9002(98)00673-1 | pages=475–478| bibcode=1998NIMPA.413..475P | url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/354107 }}</ref> (1997), which consists in the functional recovery of the silicon detectors exposed to heavy radiation.
On 1 March 2004 he was appointed professor at the University of Bern. From 2006 to 2009 he worked at the Laboratory for High Energy Physics on the design and installation of a central liquid [[argon]] system. Additionally he was deeply involved in the construction of [[cryostat]]s with high [[vacuum]] systems for [[time projection chamber]]s and design of so-called Argontube to study very long (a few meters) [[electron]] drifts in liquid argon.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ereditato | first1=A | last2=Hess | first2=M | last3=Janoŝ | first3=S | last4=Kreslo | first4=I | last5=Martinez | first5=L | last6=Messina | first6=M | last7=Moser | first7=U | last8=Rossi | first8=B | last9=Shütz | first9=H -U | last10=Zeller | first10=M | title=Study of ionization signals in a TPC filled with a mixture of liquid Argon and Nitrogen | journal=Journal of Instrumentation | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=3 | issue=10 | date=2008-10-09 | issn=1748-0221 | doi=10.1088/1748-0221/3/10/p10002 | article-number=P10002| arxiv=0808.3939 | bibcode=2008JInst...310002E | s2cid=250674670}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Rossi | first1=B | last2=Badhress | first2=I | last3=Ereditato | first3=A | last4=Haug | first4=S | last5=Hänni | first5=R | last6=Hess | first6=M | last7=Janoŝ | first7=S | last8=Juget | first8=F | last9=Kreslo | first9=I | last10=Lehmann | first10=S | last11=Lutz | first11=P | last12=Mathieu | first12=R | last13=Messina | first13=M | last14=Moser | first14=U | last15=Nydegger | first15=F | last16=Schütz | first16=H U | last17=Weber | first17=M S | last18=Zeller | first18=M | title=A prototype liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber for the study of UV laser multi-photonic ionization | journal=Journal of Instrumentation | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=4 | issue=7 | date=2009-07-13 | issn=1748-0221 | doi=10.1088/1748-0221/4/07/p07011 | article-number=P07011| arxiv=0906.3437 | bibcode=2009JInst...4.7011R | s2cid=250668322 }}</ref> He retired on 1 February 2009.

== Awards ==
In 1988 he was the co-recipient of the Prize of Slovak Academy of Sciences for the applications of point-contact spectroscopy below 1K.
In 2003 he was awarded [[Dionýz Ilkovič]] Honorary Badge of the Slovak Academy of Sciences for his achievements in low temperature physics and for the development of superconducting detectors for particle physics.

In 2009 he was awarded the Gold Medal of the Faculty of Science of the Pavol Jozef Šafárik University in Košice for his contribution to the development of the faculty, the establishment of the Low Temperature Laboratory and for his efforts in education.
At the occasion of the 40-th anniversary of the Institute of Experimental Physics SAS in Košice, he obtained the Gold Badge for his contributions to the scientific development of the Institute of Experimental Physics, SAS.

Štefan Jánoš is honorary member of the Slovak Physical Society.
